name: WD 1111+552
description: WD 1111+552 is the central star of the Owl Nebula, about 811 parsecs away.

radius.source: González-Santamaría et al. (2021), A&A 656, A51, Table 8: log(L/Lsun) = 1.98 from the star's V magnitude at its Gaia EDR3 distance, and log(Teff) = 4.97; the paper prints no radius, and 0.0374 solar radii is the sphere that radiates that luminosity at that temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann law)

temperature.source: González-Santamaría et al. (2021), A&A 656, A51, Table 8: log(Teff) = 4.97, a temperature from the literature the paper compiles; spectral type DAO

gravity.source: Napiwotzki (1999), arXiv:astro-ph/9908181, Table 2: log g from a fit of the star's spectrum

distance.source: Chornay & Walton (2021), A&A 656, A110; CDS J/A+A/656/A110, Table A.1, PN G148.4+57.0: distance 811 pc (782 to 842) from the Gaia EDR3 parallax of this star, the distance its nebula's page stands at

text.card: WD 1111+552 is the central star of the Owl Nebula, about 811 parsecs away.
text.introduction: The Owl's central star shines at 93,000 K with 95 times the Sun's light. Its sphere is about four times Earth's size.

notes: The star's mass is not measured. Evolutionary tracks give 0.55 solar masses from its spectrum (Napiwotzki (1999), arXiv:astro-ph/9908181, Table 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9908181).
A fit of its spectrum gives 93,900 K (Napiwotzki (1999), arXiv:astro-ph/9908181, Table 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9908181).

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 843950873117830528 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 300,000 of its distance per century
